title: Remove the Outermost Parentheses

concept.title: A primitive piece is a piece where the depth returns to zero
body: A balanced bracket word can be cut into **primitive** pieces: a piece is primitive if it is balanced and cannot be split into two balanced non-empty parts (`(()())` is primitive; `()()` consists of two primitive pieces). In every primitive piece the first `(` and its matching `)` are the **outermost** pair.
Walk along the word with a depth counter. A `(` is outermost exactly when the depth is **0 before** it; a `)` is outermost exactly when the depth is **0 after** it. Keep all other brackets.
Check the depth **before** counting for `(` and **after** counting for `)`; swapping them is the typical mistake. If everything is removed, print `empty`.

statement: A balanced word of parentheses is split into primitive pieces (balanced pieces that cannot be split further). From every primitive piece remove its outermost pair of parentheses, and join the results. Print the new word, or `empty` if nothing remains.
inputFormat: A single balanced word of `(` and `)`.

examples.note: Both pieces lose their only pair: empty.

hints: Track the current depth with a counter.
An opening bracket is outermost when the depth is 0 before it.
A closing bracket is outermost when the depth is 0 after it.

explanation: An opening bracket at depth 0 and a closing bracket that brings the depth back to 0 are the outermost ones; all other brackets are kept.
